$comment: Canonical cross-engine contract cases. Each case is expressible in BOTH engines' native input models and stays inside their documented shared scope: no self-employment, QBI, S-corp, retirement-plan, SEHI, HSA, IRA/401(k) adjustment, Social Security, senior/blind, student-loan, Schedule 1-A, or Additional-Medicare-triggering inputs (all of those are one-engine features — see capabilities/registry.json). Wages are kept below the Additional Medicare thresholds because the JS engine models that tax and the Python engine does not. Itemized cases are TY2025-only because the JS engine models the TY2026 charitable 0.5% AGI floor and the Sec. 68-style 2/37 limitation, which the Python engine does not.

tolerances.$comment: The Python engine rounds every line item to whole dollars (IRS half-up) as it goes; the JS engine computes in floats and rounds at display. Accumulated per-line rounding can differ by a few dollars on derived totals, so dollar quantities compare within +/- 5. Rates compare within 0.005 (effective rate is defined for comparison as total_federal_tax / AGI on both sides). Marginal ordinary rates must match exactly; cases are deliberately kept off bracket boundaries.

cases.description: Single, wages + interest, standard deduction, refund position
MFJ, wages + interest + qualified dividends, two CTC children, standard deduction
Single, high income: NIIT triggered, CTC fully phased out, 15%/20% LTCG stacking
MFJ itemized: SALT under cap, mortgage, charity below 60% AGI, medical above the 7.5% floor; balance due
Single: ST loss absorbs LT gain, net loss beyond the $3,000 limit is capped identically in both engines (carryforward tracking differs and is out of contract scope)
TY2026 (provisional ruleset in Python): single, wages + Roth conversion + IRA distribution, standard deduction
TY2026 MFJ: modest wages with LTCG and qualified dividends largely inside the 0% band
